title: Garage Door Preventive Maintenance Checklist Form
subtitle: Control inspection, stored-energy control, repair, balance, safety testing, and release through verified identity, domain-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exception ownership, and accountable closeout.
description: An original, workflow-complete garage door service preventive maintenance checklist for doors, tracks, springs, cables, operators, controls, and safety devices. It connects manufacturer information and approved safety scope to present conditions, repeatable evidence, decisions, unresolved work, and the receiving party's handoff.
use_case: Use when a qualified garage-door service technician must perform scheduled garage door service maintenance against an identified plan while preserving readings, defects, deferrals, verification, and the next due event.

blocks.label: Pre-maintenance access and control readiness
items: Door, operator, remotes, and controls isolated against unexpected movement
Torsion, extension, counterbalance, and suspended-door energy controlled
People, pets, vehicles, and property cleared from the door path
Door weight supported before spring, cable, roller, track, or bracket work
Ladder, lift, tool, winding-bar, and access method appropriate and inspected
Structural attachments, header, track supports, and fasteners assessed
Photoelectric, edge, force, reversal, release, and control functions preserved
Replacement spring, cable, roller, hardware, and operator compatibility verified

Wall control, remotes, keypad, emergency release, lock, and manual operation
Header, framing, ceiling attachment, vehicle clearance, and surrounding property

sections.title: Garage Door preventive service tasks and controlled materials
sections.guidance: Separate tasks completed from tasks merely considered, and preserve product, part, quantity, and removed-item custody.

blocks.label: Preventive maintenance tasks completed
items: Secure and support the door before controlled work
Repair or replace approved spring, cable, roller, hinge, or fixture
Align and secure tracks and structural attachments
Balance door and verify manual operating effort
Repair, adjust, or replace approved operator component
Align and test photoelectric or edge protection
Set limits and forces using approved procedure
Test wall control, remote, keypad, and emergency release
Complete obstruction, reversal, balance, and full-cycle tests
Explain safe operation, testing, and maintenance to the customer

sections.title: Garage Door measurements and post-maintenance verification
sections.guidance: Use repeatable observations to show the maintained scope reached the stated condition.

blocks.label: Measurement and verification log
blocks.guidance: Applicable measurement concepts include: Door width, height, thickness, or weight basis, Spring, cable, drum, or hardware identifier, Door balance or manual operating effort, Photo-eye height, alignment, or status, Operator force, limit, travel, or cycle result, Obstruction, reversal, release, and stop response.

blocks.label: Post-maintenance condition and function checks
items: Door remains supported and travels without binding or uncontrolled drift
Springs, cables, drums, fixtures, tracks, and fasteners are secure
Door is acceptably balanced for manual operation
Operator limits and travel stop at the intended positions
Photoelectric or edge protection responds to obstruction
Required contact or force reversal test passes
Emergency release and manual operation are functional
Customer received safe-use, periodic-test, and restriction information

Approved parts and compatibility reference
Door balance and manual-force result
Operator limit and force settings
Photoelectric or edge-device test
Obstruction and reversal test result
Emergency release and full-cycle demonstration

sections.title: Garage Door defect containment and corrective-action routing
sections.guidance: A preventive checklist does not release an unsafe, unverified, or out-of-scope condition.

blocks.label: Garage Door exception and stop-work indicators
items: Door, spring, cable, fixture, or counterbalance energy not controlled
Door cannot be independently supported during work
Track, header, bracket, ceiling, or structural attachment is damaged or uncertain
Cable fray, spring crack, bottom-fixture damage, or uncontrolled movement observed
Photoelectric, edge, force, reversal, or emergency-release protection fails
Door is unbalanced, binds, drifts, falls, or requires excessive manual force
Operator, wiring, grounding, control, or power condition is unsafe
People, pets, vehicles, or property cannot be kept clear of the travel path
Replacement component compatibility or manufacturer procedure is uncertain
Customer requests bypass, disabling, or release without required safety protection
blocks.guidance: Select the observed condition; do not use a generic exception when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Garage Door preventive maintenance checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: This garage door service preventive maintenance checklist is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, licensing, product labeling, manufacturer instructions, site policy, safety requirements, or professional judgment. Stop affected work, access, application, operation, testing, or release when spring, cable, door support, operator, entrapment protection, balance, structural attachment, electrical, or controlled-energy condition is uncertain. A garage-door safety supervisor must review the exception, authorize the controlling decision, and preserve its evidence before closeout.
